text: To describe a square on a given straight-line. Let $AB$ be the given straight-line. So it is required to describe a square on the straight-line $AB$.
Let $AC$ have been drawn at right-angles to the straight-line $AB$ from the point $A$ on it [Prop.~1.11],
and let $AD$ have been made equal to $AB$ [Prop.~1.3].
And let $DE$ have been drawn through point $D$ parallel to $AB$ [Prop.~1.31],
and let $BE$ have been drawn through point $B$ parallel to $AD$ [Prop.~1.31].
Thus, $ADEB$ is a parallelogram.
Therefore, $AB$ is equal to $DE$,
and $AD$ to $BE$ [Prop.~1.34].
But, $AB$ is equal to $AD$.
Thus, the four (sides) $BA$, $AD$, $DE$, and $EB$ are equal to one another.
assertion: the four sides BA, AD, DE, EB are equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the four (sides) $BA$, $AD$, $DE$, and $EB$ are equal to one another

text: Thus, the parallelogram $ADEB$ is equilateral.
So I say that (it is) also right-angled.
For since the straight-line $AD$ falls across the parallels $AB$ and $DE$, the (sum of the) angles $BAD$ and $ADE$ is equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.29].
assertion: sum of angles BAD and ADE equals two right-angles

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the straight-line $AD$ falls across the parallels $AB$ and $DE$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (sum of the) angles $BAD$ and $ADE$ is equal to two right-angles

text: But $BAD$ (is a) right-angle.
Thus, $ADE$ (is) also a right-angle.
And for parallelogrammic figures, the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another [Prop.~1.34].
assertion: in parallelograms opposite sides and angles are equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: for parallelogrammic figures, the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another

text: Thus, each of the opposite angles $ABE$ and $BED$ (are) also right-angles.
assertion: opposite angles ABE and BED are each right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: each of the opposite angles $ABE$ and $BED$ (are) also right-angles

text: Thus, $ADEB$ is right-angled.
And it was also shown (to be) equilateral.
assertion: ADEB was also shown to be equilateral

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: it was also shown (to be) equilateral

text: Thus, ($ADEB$) is a square [Def.~1.22].
And it is described on the straight-line $AB$.
assertion: the square is described on AB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: it is described on the straight-line $AB$

text: (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
